label: sim-cc-lexer-struggling-2
assignment: Ad-hoc Lexer for a Calculator Language
source: simulated demo student (persona: struggling) run through the real platform

viva.summary: The student understands the lexer’s purpose, can explain key loops, correctly predicts output for whitespace input, and can propose a reasonable modification for a new token type.

rubric.revise_next: Next, practice writing the exact code changes (including proper character comparison) to solidify your modification skills.

questions.answer: Ye line bas check karti hai ke agla character number hai ya nahi. I < len(src) is liye zaroori hai taake code crash na ho jaye, waise bhi ye 5 return karega.
questions.feedback: Correctly explained that the check prevents out‑of‑range access and ensures the character is a digit.
questions.prompt: In the line `while i < len(src) and src[i].isdigit():` what is its purpose in the tokenizer and why is the `i < len(src)` check necessary?

questions.answer: Mujhe lagta hai ye empty list return karega kyunke code mein shayad spaces ko skip karne ka function nahi hai.
questions.feedback: Accurately predicted that tokenizing only spaces returns an empty list.

questions.answer: Bas else ke block ko badal kar, agar char==' ;' ho to tokens.append(('SEMICOLON',char)) rakh dein, aur phir i +=1; is tarah ';' ko error na samjhayenge, lekin humne brackets aur whitespace handling ko same rakhna hai.
questions.feedback: Provided a valid approach to add a SEMICOLON token, though the syntax description could be clearer.
questions.prompt: Suppose we need the lexer to treat a semicolon ';' as a separate token type `SEMICOLON` instead of `ERROR`. How would you modify the existing `tokenize` function to handle this new requirement?

messages.body: Mera code error de raha hai, samajh nahi aa raha kyun. Kya check karun?

Aapka code 'tokenz' ko print karne ki koshish kar raha hai jo define nahi hai, isliye NameError aata hai. Is line ko comment ya correct variable name se replace kar dein, phir dobara chalayein. Kya aap ab code ko run kar ke dekhenge?
messages.hint: The error means Python tried to use a name that hasn't been defined; check the spelling of the variable you print.
